text: This poses a challenge because these devices typically have weak security and can be exploited by attackers, for example, in a distributed denial-of-service attack to flood systems and disrupt operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA and CSA have been working closely to address these challenges and to educate users about these risks and the precautions that they can take to secure their devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The scheme will raise consumer awareness on more secure products and aims to encourage manufacturers to adopt additional cybersecurity safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will improve baseline standards for such devices and will be a prerequisite to attaining the cybersecurity label.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Together, IMDA and CSA will be launching a joint Public Consultation to seek feedback on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, IMDA will also be publishing an IoT Cyber Security Guide to offer enterprise users and their vendors better guidance on the deployment of IoT technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA has made good progress since the launch of the national Cybersecurity Strategy in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But the Government alone cannot secure our cyberspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA will continue to work with individuals and businesses to enhance Singapore's cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about CSA's role in the Public Sector Data Security Review Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA works closely with other Government agencies to enhance public sector data security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, while related, data security and cybersecurity are different.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data security is concerned about the protection of data, whether this data is collected online or not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On the other hand, cybersecurity is concerned with the protection of systems, including, for example, train signalling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To Ms Sylvia Lim's point on vendor management, organisations are ultimately responsible for their obligations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These obligations continue when they decide to outsource certain functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If they do so, they should perform due diligence to select the right third party providers with proven track records and maintain sufficient oversight over this outsourcing of functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling that data is critical in this digital age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data needs to be secure and interoperable to unlock its potential, to support innovation and to benefit consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Trusted Data Sharing Framework introduced in June 2019 laid the groundwork for data interoperability and provided a common language as well as contractual templates to help organisations in Singapore share data in a trusted manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Internationally, Singapore is contributing to common data protection principles, for example, the ASEAN Framework on Digital Data Governance as well as the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Cross-Border Privacy Rules and their Privacy Recognition for Processors Systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On Ms Tin Pei Ling's questions on data centres, Singapore’s data centre market is expected to grow about 5% annually until 2024, according to a 2019 report by Cushman and Wakefield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are mindful about the environmental impact of these data centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As part of our nationwide efforts to combat climate change, IMDA is working with EDB to improve the efficiency of these data centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon and Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked about Singapore's data protection regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we generate and store more data online, it is essential that our regulations enable the innovative, legitimate use of data and simultaneously safeguard consumer interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The collection, use and disclosure of personal data are regulated by laws like PDPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes personal data shared among organisations and data collected through facial recognition technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Personal data must be protected and used for reasonable purposes, like security, as mentioned by Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Conversely, the example cited by Mr Ong Teng Koon of the sale of personal data to other organisations without consent would be in breach of the PDPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Organisations are responsible for expunging the personal data when it no longer serves the purposes for which it was collected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Public agencies are held to similar standards under the Public Sector (Governance) Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The guides will include best practices and policies on the end-to-end management of data collected via such technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For online consent agreements, PDPA continues to apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Organisations must ensure that online consent agreements are clear and spell out the reasonable purposes for which the individuals’ consent is being sought.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: PDPC also updated the Guide to Notification last year, providing organisations examples of how to utilise just-in-time notifications and obtain dynamic consent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This allows individuals to make informed decisions as and when relevant, instead of one-off lengthy consent agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As part of the effort to continually support data-driven innovation and to strengthen the accountability of these organisations and consumer trust, the Government is reviewing PDPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I announced on 28 February 2020 that the Government will be sharing more data with businesses and researchers to spur innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we do so, the high standards of data protection that the Government imposes on itself must be extended to third parties using three guiding principles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, the data is shared with these non-Government entities (NGEs) only when there is a specified purpose that will benefit the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, as a general rule, only de-identified data is shared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, access controls and safeguards should be spelt out in contracts with these NGEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Protecting our citizens online includes shielding consumers from scam calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope this will help consumers better identify international spoof calls and reject them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will continue to develop additional measures to combat scams so that our citizens can be better protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Vikram Nair asked about measures to guard against deliberate online falsehoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These can threaten our multiculturalism and the harmony of our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must protect our social cohesion in the real world and online to uphold the shared values of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will do so together with a range of partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One timely development is NUS' decision to establish a Centre for Trusted Internet and Community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Centre will research how societies discern online harms and how to build responsible public discourse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will be an important academic complement to existing efforts that nurture healthy, well-informed and inclusive online activity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Technological disruptions have changed how we work, creating new roles and new manpower demands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will continue to support all Singaporeans to capitalise on these opportunities and to meet industry needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about tech talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must work with stakeholders to expand our talent pool and strengthen career developmental pathways for emerging roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To grow our workforce, we have collaborations with the private sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are very glad that industry, for example, Apple and Alibaba collaborate with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA has been collaborating with them to develop programmes for secondary school students to help them develop some experience in marketing and pitching business ideas as they develop the technological skills, applying some of these skills to problems that interest them; for example, waste identification and recyclable materials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These industry-led programmes allow young minds in Singapore to develop technological skills, contribute to the causes that they find meaningful and prepare themselves for their future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will have to continue to make sure all Singaporeans, including those who did not learn tech skills in schools, are supported as they take on these technology-based roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will actively groom the innovation talent through mentorships, overseas attachments and structured training to position Singapore as a digital hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under SkillsFuture, the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) initiative supports professionals to upgrade their skills for the Digital Economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These programmes include the Company-Led Training (CLT) and the Cyber Security Associates and Technologists (CSAT) programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These support the transition of both ICT professionals as well as non-ICT professionals into technology-based jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, they provide an opportunity for people who are in a technology-based profession to shift their skillset, shift their career focus as well as people who have not had specific ICT training to develop ICT skills and move into a technology-based job.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Not just the companies, not just the Government, but also our trade associations are also actively contributing to these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under the Career Compass initiative, experienced ICT mentors from the Singapore Computer Society partnered Workforce Singapore (WSG) to provide career guidance to aspiring technology professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SGTech also manages Professional Conversion Programmes with platform companies, such as Salesforce, to train and place workers into new roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These new roles include examples, such as data protection officers (DPOs) and cybersecurity professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are many new jobs and exciting opportunities that are being created, and we have to increase our effort to support the professional development in these new roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Mr Patrick Tay on the need to upskill these DPOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As he noted, the PDPCs DPO Competency Roadmap and Training Framework aims to support this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I encourage more workers to tap on such training to deepen their skills in data protection and seize the opportunities in this growing field.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other than data protection, cybersecurity, as we have discussed, is a critical enabler for digitalisation and we will need more cybersecurity professionals to protect our cyberspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will build a pipeline of cybersecurity professionals to support Singapore's ambition to be a cybersecurity hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, CSA will work with the cybersecurity community and educators to nurture young Singaporeans with an aptitude in cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will provide participants with an arena for cyber sparring for mentorship for customised training and some support to participate in overseas competitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will equip these leaders to secure their organisations more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore's cybersecurity workforce is important not just for the development of a competitive digital economy, but also for our national security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To Ms Sylvia Lim's query on how CSA ensures that it has the expertise and knowledge for its mission, CSA has a Cybersecurity Professional Scheme and a Cybersecurity Competency Framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Together, these guide the professional development of our officers and allow CSA to attract and retain people with the right skillsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, I have spoken about MCI's efforts to secure our digital infrastructure to protect our cohesive society and to support all workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With this approach, we can seize the digital opportunities and embrace digitalisation with confidence together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is MCI's mission to ensure this digital future is also a brighter one for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In my speech, I will address three key strategies to realise this goal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, help citizens get more out of the digital economy by improving last-mile delivery infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, strengthen social cohesion by making trusted information widely available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And third, help all citizens to be digitally connected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad talked about disruption and future prospects for post as well as parcels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members would recall SingPost had a number of service lapses in 2018 and early 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are in a different place this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SingPost has been improving service delivery since 2019 to rebuild public trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have extended delivery hours for peak periods, improved staff remuneration and also hired more postmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SingPost's stronger performance reflects the efforts they have put in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCI and IMDA will continue to work closely with SingPost to enhance its service delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad also asked about the future prospects of the postal industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Singapore, the popularity of e-commerce has led to a steady increase in parcel deliveries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But given Singapore's urban context and consumers' busy lifestyles, doorstep deliveries often mean missed deliveries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our postal infrastructure must evolve to offer practical alternatives to doorstep deliveries so that all logistics service providers, and not just SingPost, can overcome this costly challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will complement existing commercial locker stations and doorstep deliveries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Users can collect their parcels on their way to work, or on their way home, any time of the day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Merchants and logistics service providers will also enjoy greater delivery efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This may result in more competitive delivery prices for consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA has received strong support from major e-commerce marketplaces like Qoo10 and Shopee, and logistics service providers like Qxpress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA will also partner SingPost to leverage its extensive postal service experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As we strengthen infrastructure, we must also safeguard our social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We believe all citizens should have access to trusted information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, our media industry creates compelling content for its audiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCI supports the growth of the media sector so that it stays ahead of the curve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, our Government communications are always centred on citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCI varies the modes of engagement, using face-to-face and multilingual communications to connect with all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The media industry plays a significant role in keeping citizens well-informed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how Public Service Broadcasting (PSB) can continue to be relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PSB has evolved alongside citizens' consumption preferences by providing customised content across multiple platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, Mediacorp's vernacular programmes are taking a multi-platform approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To widen audience engagement, Vasantham brought the Deepavali Countdown Show 2019 directly to audiences in Little India.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Viewers were able to celebrate in Little India with the "live" show, and catch the telecast on meWatch and Vasantham's social media platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Tech-savvy younger audiences can also enjoy more online content tailored for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA is partnering popular digital platforms, such as The Smart Local and Viddsee, to produce a wide range of drama programmes and documentaries, which will be available this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Darryl David also asked about plans to develop the media industry amid competition from over-the-top (OTT) media services, such as Netflix.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Skills Framework for Media maps out career pathways and skills in emerging trends, such as immersive media, to help media professionals stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA is also helping local media content go global.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am glad to see the rise of "made with Singapore" content in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One example is the drama series "Food Lore" by homegrown company Bert Pictures and prominent directors in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The drama has sparkled on the international stage and done us proud.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through initiatives like the Capability Partnership Programme, IMDA will continue to collaborate with global players, such as Facebook and CJ ENM Hong Kong, and strengthen the expertise of local media companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how the Government ensures timely access to information for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This brings me to my second point on citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are strengthening last-mile engagement to connect with citizens face-to-face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of the SG Ambassadors is Mr Kong Seet Kiang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Already 70 years old, he has been volunteering three days a week since 2015 and a familiar face among Bukit Timah seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MGP roadshows are also in full swing in the heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the deep involvement of the community, the Government has engaged nearly 200,000 MG seniors and their families at over 200 roadshows and events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Good translation is essential for important messages to reach all segments of Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCI's Translation Department (TD) undertakes the most important pieces of translation work for the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It also champions high standards when it comes to translated work produced by all public agencies, whether done inhouse or outsourced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, MCI initiated various moves to boost our translation capabilities, producing increasing quantities of translated materials, at good quality and at speed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Centre of Excellence will drive three key workstreams: talent, technology and partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we will groom translation talents and upskill industry practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is done through programmes like the MCI Information Service (Translation) Scholarship and the Translation Talent Development Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we use technology to improve the speed and quality of Government translation work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As SG Translate produces translations that suit the local context, it is more accurate than other machine translation tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck asked how we are involving more partners to enhance translation technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From 2021, MCI will invite selected groups, including businesses and schools, to submit quality translations through a web portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The more quality inputs we receive, the more data for training the engine, and the stronger the technology’s underlying AI will become.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will open up the web portal progressively to more users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will benefit more practitioners while also growing the engine’s capability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, MCI is also strengthening partnerships to close translation gaps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, we are working with organisations with skilled translators to meet periodic surges in translation demand within the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also have retainer arrangements to boost vetting capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Here, I want to say a very big "thank you" to our translation partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is so much more we can do together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us continue our partnership to ensure strong Government communications for our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If translation is the bridge to connect our multiracial communities, then preserved records open a window to Singapore's shared heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To strengthen cohesiveness, we must remember the shared history that binds us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB and the National Archives of Singapore (NAS) are widening public access to national and social memories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the ongoing Legal Deposit display at Bedok Public Library, Singaporeans can access a vast array of publications from yesteryear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of them is the book "Assembly Songs", a valuable compilation of school songs of the past.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the updated NLB Act empowering NLB to archive digital materials, NLB has also added 40,000 Singapore websites to its digital collection, preserved for generations to enjoy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NAS will be launching a crowdsourcing initiative to capture treasured sights and sounds of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Citizens can play a part by contributing under categories, such as "Sounds of the Heartlands" and "Festivals and Celebrations".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Anchored by our past, we can face the future with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To bring Singapore forward, Minister Iswaran said all citizens should feel confident about seizing digital opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Digitalisation has disrupted industries, transforming jobs and creating new ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The demand for high-skilled roles is set to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will create new opportunities for the workforce in roles, such as product managers, data scientists and software engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We must support all workers in skills transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One segment the Government is focusing on is mid-career professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With digitalisation creating disruption alongside opportunities, this group of professionals may face challenges in career transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, their rich experience makes them invaluable to the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme supports workers to acquire new ICT skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, 50-year-old Mr Tan Wai Chong worked in the IT field for 25 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He has always been interested to learn new skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With structured training from PSA through TeSA’s CLT programme, he took on an advanced tech role.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He is now an Application Developer with PSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To support more mid-career professionals like Mr Tan, IMDA is launching the TeSA Mid-Career Advance programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The programme will comprise training and mentorship of up to 24 months to equip mid-career professionals with competencies for in-demand tech roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For a start, about 10 companies have come on board and committed to about 500 training placements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA aims to benefit an additional 2,000 mid-career professionals over the next two to three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together with the industry, we will support these professionals to further their careers with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, some segments of the population, such as seniors and low-income households, may feel lost in the digital society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We must overcome age, income and literacy gaps so that everyone can reap the benefits of the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about measures to boost digital readiness, while Dr Teo Ho Pin asked how we are improving digital access for low-income households and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB and IMDA are galvanising the community and industry to build digital literacy and skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is in sync with the Singapore Together movement, where the Government partners Singaporeans to build a better future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of the beneficiaries is Mr D Rashpal Singh Sidhu.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With subsidised broadband, Mr Sidhu found a part-time job after searching online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He also uses the Internet to stay in touch with overseas relatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, while household broadband access in Singapore has increased over the years, some low-income households are still unconnected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also helping seniors to learn digital skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA, together with partners, such as NLB, organised over 200 free Digital Clinics in libraries and community spaces to help seniors with their smartphone devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some 3,000 volunteers have reached out to over 15,000 seniors island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of these seniors is 64-year-old Madam Safia Bte Mohd Salleh.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through Digital Clinics, she discovered useful apps to make polyclinic and hospital appointments and check the arrival times of buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: She plans to visit Digital Clinics again to learn more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are also ground-up efforts to help children navigate the online environment safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is important as they are increasingly exposed to technology from an early age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Media Literacy Council is partnering Google to bring a mobile interactive exhibition on online safety to primary schools this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Students can learn about online safety, cyberbullying and the actions to take when encountering problems online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness also supports community efforts to combat online risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, a group of NTU students organised an exhibition to raise awareness of online child grooming.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Visitors could step into the shoes of victims through interactive installations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It was very well done, and the messages hit home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I applaud the strong contributions of the community to promote online safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our march towards the digital future must also be matched by an unwavering sense of community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the fast-moving digital world, it is more important than ever to connect people through common spaces and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our libraries play a key role in this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have transformed over the years to become trusted and treasured spaces where people can bond, socialise and learn.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Cedric Foo asked how we are revamping libraries to ensure they stay relevant in a digital world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have revamped six libraries under the Libraries of the Future initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Strong community engagement to encourage lifelong learning is the hallmark of these libraries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, at library@harbourfront, which opened last year, citizens young and old can learn about emerging technology at The Tech Showcase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Interactive displays on topics like educational robotics offer an engaging learning experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Families can also participate in hands-on activities at the children's makerspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The revamped libraries have seen an increase of 73% in total visitors and 49% in total loans in the first year of operation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our libraries are an exception to the global trend of falling library usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB will revamp eight more libraries from now to 2026.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They include Choa Chu Kang Public Library, Central Public Library, Queenstown Public Library and Marine Parade Public Library.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition to these, a brand new Punggol Regional Library is in the works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These future libraries will play a stronger role in connecting Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, Punggol Regional Library will offer spaces and collections for all age groups and needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Users with disabilities and children with special needs can enjoy customised services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The library will also house a specially curated world children’s literature collection so younger Singaporeans can appreciate cultural diversity from an early age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, the digital future presents endless possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCI will persevere in our efforts to ensure every business, worker and citizen can seize digital opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to nurture enduring partnerships to realise this vision, and leave no one behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us work together, as one nation, to forge a strong digital future.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Just one clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: She mentioned that the rollout of the locker network will be overseen and managed by IMDA.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: This entity will then have a clear mandate focusing on digitising and driving innovation and transformation in the post, parcel and logistics industry in Singapore by setting relevant standards trialing and driving adoption of new innovative technology, such as, say, drone delivery and blockchain traceablility.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Within IMDA, in fact, there is already a sector transformation group whose work is to support the digitalisation as well as transformation of different industry sectors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Urban Logistics is one of them and the Nationwide Parcel Locker Network that we talked about is one of the initiatives under this particular sector.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To answer Mr Cedric Foo's question, this is a very important goal to ensure that every child in Singapore is able to learn well and is able to make the full use of the benefits of digital learning.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, we do partner MOE to also ensure that at the school level, every child who needs digital devices or computers is also being served.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: I welcome the move to set up gov.sg WhatsApp group, a WhatsApp channel to communicate with the public.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: At which point does MCI determine which channel to communicate with?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: So, what were the considerations behind choosing which platform as a third-party platform to communicate with the public?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his question.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said earlier, we have to choose the channel according to both the target segment that we want to reach out to but also in terms of our ability to respond situationally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In this case, the COVID-19 outbreak occurred very quickly, we sensed that there is going to be an immediate need for a reliable source of information for our population.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What we then did was to repurpose an existing channel, which was a WhatsApp channel that was already available, that was used for communication for certain types of information, particularly the MG package and related information, and we decided that we would repurpose it and make that an immediate mechanism by which we convey the requisite, relevant information to our population.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it has worked well, as evidenced by the response that we have seen from the subscribers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we do not preclude the possibility of using other channels.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But this was responding to an immediate need with the tool that was available to us with the shortest possible notice.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Chairman, some months ago, we had a healthy discussion between Mr Pritam Singh and myself about POFMA, whether the Judiciary is the best party to act, or whether the Executive branch is better-placed to act on the issuance of Correction Notices.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: I think the recent COVID-19 outbreak is a good example of when to use POFMA.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: From the recent experience using POFMA for this purpose, does the Minister feel even stronger now that this is a job best left for the Executive branch?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Chairman, I thank the Member, who is the Chairman of the Government Parliamentary Committee, for his comment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I emphasised, I think what COVID-19 has in particular brought to the fore, is the need for swift action, when you are trying to ensure a falsehood does not gain traction and mislead the population.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In a situation like an epidemic, it is essential that our population stays calm, gets advice and information from reliable sources, and is able to then take appropriate measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In that context, we have found POFMA, the tools and also the ability to exercise those tools, the authority that is vested in the Executive to exercise those tools, to have been very effective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It has, I think, demonstrated the case that we made in the course of the debate in introducing the legislation that one of the reasons, not the only, but a key reason for wanting to site that authority with the Executive arm, was to ensure the ability to respond decisively, swiftly given the virulence and virality of falsehoods that are pervading online.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think our COVID-19 experience has reinforced, if anything, that conviction; and certainly, we have no reason to question the reasons for doing so.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, I do not mean to open the debate that we had on POFMA again, but the position as far as the Workers' Party is concerned, is still the same.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, you have instances of fake news in the case of epidemics, even pandemics; certainly, they have to be taken down swiftly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But there are different modalities that swift action can manifest itself in.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And the Workers' Party position is that there are still other options, apart from Executive orders, that can eventuate in that outcome.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, is there anything else we can do about that?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Either future legislation or what I had suggested was better education of the population.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because, firstly, if it succeeded in terms of its reach to a large base of the population, it meant that they had a reliable source of information on COVID-19 through a channel that they are already quite accustomed to using.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we think that that is a good start.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Cedric Foo, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Chairman, indeed, digital technology will be a key enabler for a brighter future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Listening to Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and Minister Iswaran, I am sure my colleagues share my view that we are in good hands.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: That is because they do not only talk about technology and digits, they were talking about people.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
